messages:
Maya: Quick sync — draft proposal for how the API should handle concurrent multi-step external actions (fan-out/fan-in). Need decisions: default ordering, per-call timeouts, retry semantics, billing, and launch criteria. TL;DR: opt-in parallelism, explicit idempotency key, per-subcall timeout, global workflow timeout. Draft doc: https://redwood.internal/rdw/parallel-actions (proto)

Trent: +1 on opt-in. Default should remain sequential for safety.

Diego: Can we support 'preserve_order' vs 'any' ordering modes? Some customers rely on deterministic ordering.

Maya: Yes. Proposal: ordering param with values [preserve, best_effort, unordered]. preserve => results returned in request order (slower). best_effort => attempt to map back when possible. unordered => fastest first.

Sam: What about retries? At-least-once vs at-most-once? Connectors like payments want at-least-once with dedupe keys.

Ellie: Exactly — require 'idempotency_key' per subcall. System will retry up to N times on transient errors. For at-most-once expensive ops, customers must set 'disable_retries'.

Diego: Timeout semantics? per_subcall_timeout + global_workflow_timeout. If subcall hits per_subcall_timeout => cancel and return error for that branch, but continue others? Or fail whole workflow?

Maya: Default: fail-fast if critical flag set, otherwise fan-in collects partial results and attaches per-branch statuses. See config example:

```
parallel_config: {
  enabled: true,
  max_concurrency: 4,
  ordering: "preserve",
  per_subcall_timeout_ms: 3000,
  global_timeout_ms: 12000,
  retry_policy: { max_attempts: 2, backoff_ms: 200 }
}
```

Trent: Need clear failure model in API docs. Also add metrics: per-branch latency, retry_count, partial_failure_rate.

Sam: Billing — do we bill for every attempted subcall or only successful? Customers will ask. Recommend bill for attempts (consumed infra) but surface 'billed_attempts' vs 'successful_calls' in usage reports.

Ellie: Launch criteria: docs + SDKs, E2E with sample connectors (http, sql, stripe), canary with 5% of traffic on hosted, perf SLO: 95th tail for preserved-order <= baseline *2.

Maya: Owners: Maya (product), Diego (spec + connectors), Ellie (SDK + docs), Trent (SRE + rollout). Action: Diego to PR spec by EOD Friday. Any objections?

Trent: No objections. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled for 1751230000 — will create canary channel.
